learning_goal: Name the three parts of the small intestine and say which is fixed and which is mobile, walk the four parts of the duodenum and their relations, tell jejunum from ileum on six features at a spotter table, follow the superior mesenteric artery to the gut it supplies, and explain how the wall is built for absorption.

structures.name: duodenum
structures.label: Duodenum
structures.narration: Twelve finger-breadths long, hence the name, and shaped like a letter C lying on its back around the head of the pancreas. Only its first inch is mobile; the rest is secondarily retroperitoneal, plastered to the posterior wall, which is why it does not have a mesentery and does not move. It is the junction of two embryological guts: everything above the entry of the bile duct is foregut and coeliac territory, everything below is midgut and superior mesenteric territory. That single line explains the whole of its blood supply and the referral of its pain.

structures.name: jejunum
structures.label: Jejunum
structures.narration: The upper two fifths of the mobile small bowel, lying mostly in the upper left quadrant. Pick it up and it is thick-walled, wide, and deep red because it is well supplied. Its mesentery is almost fat-free near the gut, so you can see through the windows between the vessels, and its vasa recta are long and straight, arising from only one or two arcades. Its mucosal folds — the plicae circulares — are tall and closely set, which is what makes the jejunum the main site of absorption and what makes obstructed jejunum look like a stack of coins on a plain film.

structures.name: ileum
structures.label: Ileum
structures.narration: The lower three fifths, lying mostly in the pelvis and the right iliac fossa, ending at the ileocaecal junction. It is thinner, narrower and paler than jejunum, its mesentery is loaded with fat right up to the bowel wall so there are no windows, and its vasa recta are short and arise from four or five tiers of arcades. Its folds are low and sparse. Its distinguishing feature is lymphoid: Peyer's patches on the antimesenteric border, which is where typhoid ulcerates and perforates. The last few centimetres — the terminal ileum — are the only place in the body that absorbs vitamin B12 and bile salts, so resect them and you get megaloblastic anaemia and fatty stools.

structures.name: superior mesenteric artery
structures.label: Superior mesenteric artery
structures.narration: The artery of the midgut, leaving the front of the aorta at L1, one centimetre below the coeliac trunk. It passes forward over the third part of the duodenum and enters the root of the mesentery, giving twelve to fifteen jejunal and ileal branches from its left side and the ileocolic and colic branches from its right. Because the whole midgut hangs on this one artery, an embolus into it kills bowel from the duodenojejunal flexure to two thirds of the way along the transverse colon — pain out of all proportion to the physical signs.

structures.name: superior mesenteric vein
structures.label: Superior mesenteric vein
terms: on the right of the artery
structures.narration: Runs up the root of the mesentery on the right of its artery and joins the splenic vein behind the neck of the pancreas to form the portal vein. Everything absorbed from the small intestine except the long-chain fats goes to the liver first. The fats go into lacteals instead, up the thoracic duct, and reach the blood at the root of the neck — which is why they bypass the liver's first pass entirely.

structures.name: pancreatic duct
structures.label: Pancreatic duct & the ampulla
structures.narration: The main pancreatic duct joins the bile duct and the two open together on the major duodenal papilla, halfway down the posteromedial wall of the second part of the duodenum. That common channel is the hepatopancreatic ampulla, guarded by the sphincter of Oddi. It explains gallstone pancreatitis: a stone impacted at the ampulla blocks pancreatic outflow as well as bile, and the patient gets jaundice and pancreatitis together.

structures.name: gallbladder
structures.label: Gallbladder & biliary drainage
structures.narration: Bile is stored here and delivered to the second part of the duodenum through the bile duct. Ninety-five per cent of the bile salts released are reabsorbed in the terminal ileum and sent back to the liver — the enterohepatic circulation. That is a closed loop running the length of the small intestine, and cutting either end of it breaks fat absorption.

structures.name: appendix
structures.label: Appendix — the end of the road
structures.narration: The ileum ends by opening into the caecum in the right iliac fossa, and the appendix hangs from the caecum just below that opening. Use the appendix to find the junction: the three taeniae of the caecum converge on its base. Two conditions live at this corner and are easily confused with appendicitis — ileocaecal tuberculosis, which is common in Nigeria, and a Meckel's diverticulum, which sits two feet proximal to the valve on the antimesenteric border of the ileum in about two per cent of people.

structures.name: stomach
structures.label: Stomach
structures.narration: Delivers chyme through the pylorus a few millilitres at a time. The small intestine never receives a meal in one go, which is what allows an organ a few centimetres wide to handle it.

structures.name: liver
structures.label: Liver
structures.narration: Sits above and in front of the duodenum and receives everything the small bowel absorbs, by way of the portal vein.

structures.name: right kidney
structures.label: Right kidney
structures.narration: The hilum of the right kidney lies directly behind the second part of the duodenum. So does the right ureter. Both are at risk in surgery on that part, and both explain why duodenal disease can produce back pain.

structures.name: left kidney
structures.label: Left kidney
structures.narration: Lies behind the fourth part of the duodenum on the left of the aorta. The left renal vein crosses the aorta in the same fork as the third part of the duodenum, which is why an abnormally acute angle at the origin of the superior mesenteric artery compresses both.

structures.name: descending aorta
structures.label: Aorta
structures.narration: The third part of the duodenum crosses in front of the aorta at L3, held between the aorta behind and the superior mesenteric artery in front. That sandwich is the whole of superior mesenteric artery syndrome: lose the fat pad between the two vessels and the duodenum is pinched shut.

structures.name: celiac artery
structures.label: Coeliac trunk
structures.narration: Supplies the duodenum down as far as the entry of the bile duct, through the gastroduodenal and superior pancreaticoduodenal arteries. Below that line the supply comes from the superior mesenteric. The two anastomose in the pancreaticoduodenal arcade, so the duodenum is the one place where the foregut and midgut circulations meet.

structures.name: inferior mesenteric artery
structures.label: Inferior mesenteric artery
structures.narration: Included only to fix the three midline gut arteries in order: coeliac at T12 for the foregut, superior mesenteric at L1 for the midgut, inferior mesenteric at L3 for the hindgut. The small intestine belongs to the first two, never the third.

structures.name: rectum
structures.label: Rectum
structures.narration: Marks the floor of the abdomen for orientation. Coils of ileum drop into the pelvis in front of the rectum, which is why pelvic collections irritate small bowel and why free fluid gathers there first.

structures.label: Duodenojejunal flexure — the ligament of Treitz
structures.calibrated_by: geometry: CONTACT on the duodenum (FMA7206, 119.6 mm span) witnessed by the jejunum (FMA7207) at 0.53 mm. One witness only — the flexure is by definition the single place these two meshes meet end to end, so a second witness does not exist; the 0.53 mm gap is the whole of the evidence. tools/derive-landmark.mjs --parent FMA7206 --contact FMA7207
structures.narration: Where the fixed gut becomes the mobile gut, at L2 just left of the midline. The suspensory muscle of the duodenum — the ligament of Treitz — slings it from the right crus of the diaphragm. It is the surgeon's landmark for the start of the jejunum and the clinician's dividing line: bleeding above it is upper gastrointestinal and comes up as haematemesis, bleeding below it is lower. The root of the mesentery starts here and runs down to the right sacroiliac joint. Note what this marker is: a point measured where the duodenum meets the jejunum. The suspensory muscle itself has no model in the catalog and is not drawn.

structures.label: Major duodenal papilla — the ampulla of Vater
structures.calibrated_by: geometry: CONTACT on the duodenum (FMA7206, 119.6 mm span) witnessed by the pancreatic duct (FMA10419) at 1.26 mm. One witness — the duct's termination is the papilla, and no second structure in the catalog meets the duodenum here (there is no bile duct mesh). tools/derive-landmark.mjs --parent FMA7206 --contact FMA10419
structures.narration: Halfway down the posteromedial wall of the second part of the duodenum, where the bile duct and the main pancreatic duct open together through the hepatopancreatic ampulla, guarded by the sphincter of Oddi. This marker is measured from the pancreatic duct's contact with the duodenum only — the catalog has no bile duct, so the bile half of the junction is narrated and not drawn. It is the target of ERCP and the site where an impacted gallstone gives jaundice and pancreatitis at once. The minor papilla, about two centimetres above and in front of it, is not measurable here and is not marked.

structures.label: Ileocaecal junction — the end of the small bowel
structures.calibrated_by: geometry: CONTACT on the ileum (FMA7208, 201.6 mm span) witnessed by the appendix (FMA14542) at 0.95 mm. One witness — there is no caecum mesh in the catalog, so the appendix is the only structure that meets the ileum at this corner, and it hangs a couple of centimetres below the true opening; the marker is therefore the ileum's terminal end rather than the valve itself. tools/derive-landmark.mjs --parent FMA7208 --contact FMA14542
structures.narration: The end of six metres of small bowel, in the right iliac fossa. The ileocaecal valve here holds contents back long enough for the terminal ileum to absorb vitamin B12 and bile salts, and stops colonic bacteria travelling back up. Measure Meckel's from this point: two feet proximal, on the antimesenteric border. The valve itself and the caecum have no models in the catalog — this marker is the ileum's terminal end, found by its contact with the appendix, and the label says so.

views.title: Three parts, six metres
views.narration: Duodenum, jejunum, ileum — about six metres in the cadaver and rather shorter in life because of muscle tone. Divide it by mobility, not by length. The duodenum is fixed to the back wall and cannot be delivered out of a wound. The jejunum and ileum hang on a mesentery and can be run through your fingers metre by metre, which is exactly what the surgeon does looking for a perforation. The jejunum takes the upper two fifths, the ileum the lower three, and there is no line between them — only a change in character.

views.title: Walking the duodenum
views.narration: Four parts, and each is remembered by what lies behind it. The first runs back and up for five centimetres; only its first inch is intraperitoneal, and the gastroduodenal artery is behind it. The second descends on the right of L1 to L3 with the hilum of the right kidney behind and the bile and pancreatic ducts entering its posteromedial wall. The third runs left across the aorta and the inferior vena cava at L3, under the superior mesenteric vessels. The fourth ascends on the left of the aorta to L2 and turns forward at the duodenojejunal flexure, held up by the suspensory muscle of the duodenum — the ligament of Treitz — which is the surgical landmark for the start of the jejunum and the dividing line between upper and lower gastrointestinal bleeding.

views.title: Jejunum or ileum
views.narration: Six features, and you will be asked for them. Position: jejunum upper left, ileum lower right and pelvic. Wall: jejunum thick, ileum thin. Lumen: jejunum wide, ileum narrow. Folds: jejunum tall and crowded, ileum low and sparse, absent at the end. Mesentery: jejunum has clear windows and long straight vasa recta from one or two arcades, ileum is fat-laden with short vasa recta from four or five arcades. Lymphoid tissue: scattered in jejunum, aggregated into Peyer's patches in ileum. Hold a loop up to the light in theatre and the arcades alone will tell you where you are.

views.title: One artery holds the midgut

ops.kind: crosses in front of the third part

views.narration: The coeliac trunk supplies the duodenum down to the major papilla; the superior mesenteric supplies it from there onwards and every centimetre of jejunum and ileum after it. The two meet in the pancreaticoduodenal arcade, the only anastomosis between foregut and midgut supply. Within the mesentery the branches form arcades and send vasa recta to the bowel wall — and those vasa recta are end arteries. Occlude one and you get a segmental infarct, which is why a mesenteric tear matters as much as a bowel tear.

views.title: Built for absorption
views.narration: Cut across and the surface area is multiplied three times over. First the plicae circulares — permanent circular folds of mucosa and submucosa that do not flatten when the bowel distends, which is why they show as lines crossing the whole width of the bowel on a plain abdominal film. Then the villi, finger-like projections of mucosa, each with a central lacteal and a capillary net. Then the microvilli of the brush border on every enterocyte. Between the villi are the crypts of Lieberkuhn, which is where new cells are made and why the lining renews itself every few days. The duodenum adds Brunner's glands in its submucosa, secreting alkaline mucus to neutralise the acid arriving from the stomach — one of only two places in the gut with glands in the submucosa. The other is the oesophagus.

views.title: Follow it through
views.narration: Two movements, not one. Segmentation is the commoner: rings of circular muscle contract and relax at intervals, chopping the column and mixing it with bile, pancreatic juice and intestinal secretion — it moves contents almost nowhere but it is what absorption depends on. Peristalsis carries it forward, and between meals a migrating motor complex sweeps the empty bowel clean every ninety minutes or so. A meal takes three to five hours to travel from pylorus to caecum. The ileocaecal valve then holds it back long enough for the terminal ileum to take up bile salts and vitamin B12, and stops colonic bacteria coming the other way.

views.title: Where it goes wrong
views.narration: Obstruction is the classic emergency: colicky central pain, vomiting early if the block is high, distension late, and central gas shadows crossed by valvulae conniventes on the film. In Nigeria the leading causes are adhesions, strangulated external hernia and, in children, intussusception and heavy Ascaris load. Two things at the ileocaecal corner mimic appendicitis: ileocaecal tuberculosis and a Meckel's diverticulum. Learn Meckel's by the rule of twos — two per cent of people, two feet from the valve, two inches long, two tissue types, and it usually presents before the age of two. And typhoid ulcerates the Peyer's patches of the terminal ileum, so an enteric fever in the third week that suddenly develops a rigid abdomen has perforated.

gaps: The duodenum is one model. The catalog holds no separate superior, descending, horizontal or ascending part, no duodenal cap, no major or minor duodenal papilla and no duodenojejunal flexure, so beat 2 walks the four parts by tracing along the duodenum and lighting each posterior relation in turn — the bed teaches the part. Two of those named features are now marked as measured anchors rather than left to the narration: the duodenojejunal flexure and the major duodenal papilla (see below). Every part name and the ligament of Treitz are in terms[], so a note naming any of them opens this scene. Beat 2 is moded 'associated_organs', which is the mode the curriculum entry asks for and which no other beat here supplied: what it actually does is show the duodenum surrounded by the organs that bed it and drain into it.

Three landmark anchors were derived and authored at audit on 2026-08-29, closing the note that stood here: the duodenojejunal flexure (duodenum-to-jejunum contact, 0.53 mm), the major duodenal papilla (duodenum-to-pancreatic-duct contact, 1.26 mm) and the ileocaecal junction (ileum-to-appendix contact, 0.95 mm). All three emitted. Each has a single witness and that is stated in its calibrated_by, because each of these three junctions is by definition a meeting of exactly two meshes — there is no third structure in the catalog to converge on. All three carry status 'needs-review': the measurement is proved, the landing on the feature is not, and only somebody opening the scene and looking can settle that.

Two features named in beat 2 remain unmarkable and are narrated only. The minor duodenal papilla has no witness — no accessory pancreatic duct mesh exists — and the bile duct has no mesh at all, so the major papilla is measured from the pancreatic duct alone and the bile half of the ampulla is described rather than shown. The four parts of the duodenum are likewise not separable: a part of a tube is a length, not a point, and derive-landmark.mjs measures points.

There is no caecum and no colon wall of any kind in the catalog. The large-gut meshes that do exist are the three taeniae coli (FMA76891, FMA76892, FMA76893), the appendix, the rectum and the external anal sphincter — an earlier version of this note said only the appendix and the rectum, which the Large intestine scene disproved. So the ileum's ending is taught through the appendix, which hangs from the caecum a couple of centimetres below the ileocaecal opening and whose base is found by the converging taeniae. That is option (b) of the resolution rule, teaching a structure through an adjacent one that exists, and the label says what is being shown. The ileocaecal valve itself is narrated and not drawn.

No mesentery and no peritoneum. The root of the mesentery, its fifteen-centimetre oblique line from the duodenojejunal flexure to the right sacroiliac joint, the windows, and the fat encroachment that distinguishes ileum from jejunum are all narrated in beats 1 and 3 and all in terms[], but a double fold of peritoneum has no model. This is the single biggest omission in the scene, because half of the jejunum-versus-ileum answer is a statement about the mesentery. 'Peritoneum & mesentery' is its own curriculum entry, authored as a diagram-mode scene and awaiting artwork; it carries the mesentery teaching this scene has to narrate.

No pancreas mesh exists — only the pancreatic duct, FMA10419 — so the head of the pancreas, which the duodenum curves around and which is the whole reason the C is a C, is represented by the duct that runs through it. The label says so.

Villi, microvilli, crypts of Lieberkuhn, Brunner's glands and Peyer's patches are microscopic and belong to a microscopic-mode scene. They are taught here in narration because plicae circulares, villi and microvilli are one continuous idea about surface area and a student meets them together, but the corpus should carry a histology scene for the small intestine wall and this scene should link to it once it exists.

Jejunal and ileal arteries, the arcades and the vasa recta have no meshes; beat 4 traces from the aorta through the superior mesenteric artery to the two segments of bowel and narrates the arcade pattern. The pancreaticoduodenal arcade, which is the anastomosis between foregut and midgut supply, is named and not drawn.

The inferior mesenteric artery is carried as context purely to fix the T12 / L1 / L3 sequence in the student's head. It supplies no part of the small intestine, and its narration says so, so that nobody reads its presence as a claim.
